about: Generated by tools/map_layout.mjs from map/world/S4.json; never edit. Metres in the section frame: X east (out of the city in S5), D north, H up. Entities keep their map IDs; figures and trees also carry their slug as id for people.json.

assumptions: East-west and height share S5's scale, 77 px per metre; depth is 51.25 px of v per metre everywhere on the ground (S5's bridge deck). This part's real-size checks say the painter draws far things smaller (questions: the diminution up the silk); the scale is kept unchanged until the lead decides.
Painted figure size is not a scale (S5: street figures about 1.3x life; here 150-195 px on the road, 1.9-2.5 m at 77 px/m). Place by foot point.
Supports other than the ground: the seat on the front of S5's covered ox cart and the temple gate hall's plinth (supports).

datum.about: where the main road crosses the seam with S5 (u 9400): its centre-line point 0, at S5's road end (scan 9400, 1370). Station +26.05 there, the station of S5.road.main's east end, so stations run on from the gate.

trees.what: Tall slender willow behind (north of) the building east of the big willow: a thin straight trunk rising to the top of the silk with long bare whips fanning out on both sides.

Huge old willow with a massive, dark, burled and mottled bole standing in front of the east end of the fortune-teller's awning: the bole bulges out low (lumpy, moss-dotted) and the trunk leans up to the north-east to a knobby pollard head, from which long bare whips sweep out over the awning roof to the west and up to the top of the silk.
Clump of long, thin, bare whips rising from the bottom edge of the silk east of the big whip tree and fanning up to the north-east against the big south roof.

Large bare tree at the bottom edge of the silk in front of the south row's roofs: a short trunk that splits at once into many long thin bare whips, the longest sweeping far to the west over the bottom edge and others rising almost to the eaves.
Tall straight dark trunk rising behind (north of) the fortune-teller's mat awning to the top of the silk, with a few bare branches near the top; its foot is hidden by the awning.

Large bare tree with a dark, twisted, knotty trunk standing just east of the courier post's gate behind the sleeping soldiers; it forks at about mid-height into two stems, the west one rising straight up past the top of the silk, the east one leaning north-east; bare elm-like branches with knobbly twig tips spread over the courier hall.
Small shrub of dark leaf clusters at the west foot of the little bridge in front of the courier post; leaf clusters continue along the bridge's arched top like a climbing plant.
A tuft of long thin stems (tall grass, reeds or a bare bush) fanning out from one foot at the silk's bottom edge in front of the big building's slatted front.

Big old pollard willow with a thick, mottled trunk rising from the bank top just west of the sleeping soldiers to a broad knobbly head; its exposed roots run down the bank face to the road, and its long whips fan up to the top of the silk and hang down over the stake fence and the spears.
Low bush of many thin bare stems fanning up from the silk's bottom edge below the tables, under the leafy clump's east end.

Big old pollard willow with a thick gnarled trunk leaning up to the west from the bank top at the road's north edge to a knobbly head, from which long bare willow whips fan out up to the top of the silk and hang down over the road group.
Dense clump of narrow, pointed leaves in sprays (bamboo-like) around the foot of the tall bare tree, in front of the tables under the big roof's west end.

Tall leafless tree with many thin, upright, branching limbs (elm-like), rising from the bottom of the silk west of the big roof south of the road; its trunk is hidden in a leafy clump, and its crown reaches up to the road's south edge and screens the man seen from behind.
Massive old tree with a dark, knotted and hollowed trunk standing behind the east sedan chair and its rear bearer, leaning up to the north-west; its crown merges with the willow whips above.
Dense leafy shrub or small tree (small leaf clusters, unlike the willows) behind the gable of the small building south of the road.

Tall tree with two (or three) slender trunks rising together from one foot behind the west sedan chair and the canopy, branching high into gnarled dark limbs; its long hanging whips fill the top of the silk over the side road.

Willow-like tree rising from the bottom edge of the silk in front of the low building south of the road; many long thin branches and whips spread over the big tiled roof to the west and the thatched roof to the north.
Crown of thin bare-looking branches radiating from a point just above the ridge of the building east of the temple: a tree standing behind (north of) that building, its trunk hidden by the roof.

Tall tree whose dark knotty trunk rises from behind the stalls between the dark and the light parasol, forks at about two-thirds height, and climbs north-east with a crown of fan-shaped needle-like sprays (pine-like) spreading from the grove to over the pigs and up to below the temple.
Slender tree: a thin trunk leaning up to the north-west from a small forked foot on the open ground to a dark knotty head, from which sprays of needle-like strokes spread.

Old pollarded tree (willow-like): a dark, swollen, knobbly head from which long straight limbs with fan-shaped needle-like sprays spread far west over the mat awning and up the silk; its trunk is hidden behind the dark parasol and the stall.

Fans of pine-like needle clusters showing above and over the tiled roof of the house at the top of the silk (S4.bld.house_9590): one fan at the roof's west part, a broad fan rising from the roof's east eave corner with a few sprays drooping east of it over the railing, and a branch running up from that fan to the silk's top edge; the trunk is not shown (behind the house or above the top edge).

Old tree with a thick, twisting, knotty trunk (pale bark, dark knots) rising from spreading roots and leaning east into heavy limbs at about v 270; crown of fan-shaped clusters of fine needle-like strokes (pine-like) reaching up to the houses.
